sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Des Plaines, IL?
sections.html:
Des Plaines sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer on the house as it is. The choice usually turns on how much work the house needs, whether tenants live in it, and how soon a closing date has to land.

  • A traditional listing can pull strong prices in a city where the median owner-occupied home value is $335,600, but it adds showings, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • A private sale skips the commission and leaves the contract and disclosures to you.
  • A cash sale trims the timeline and works for inherited homes, rentals, and houses with deferred maintenance.

Because Des Plaines sits beside O'Hare and two tollways, buyers range from commuters to investors who want rentals near the airport and the Metra line.

sections.h2: What is Des Plaines like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Des Plaines is a Cook County city just north of O'Hare International Airport, built along the Des Plaines River. It covers about 14 square miles and had 60,675 residents at the 2020 census.

French explorers named the river for the sycamores they thought resembled European plane trees. American settlers arrived after the 1833 Treaty of Chicago, followed by German immigrants. The Chicago, St. Paul and Fond du Lac Railroad built through in 1857, the stop took the Des Plaines name in 1859, and voters converted the village to a city in 1925. Growth jumped after World War II once O'Hare opened nearby, and the population climbed from 14,994 in 1950 to 57,239 by 1970.

Today Interstates 90 and 294, U.S. Routes 12, 14 and 45, and Illinois Routes 58, 72 and 83 cross the city. Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line stops at the Des Plaines and Cumberland stations, and the Pace Pulse Dempster Line runs between Evanston and O'Hare. Major employers listed in the city's financial report include Rivers Casino, Universal Oil Products, Oakton College, Sysco, Juno Lighting, Holy Family Medical Center, Wheels Inc. and LSG Sky Chefs.

Elementary and middle school students attend Districts 62, 59 or 63, and high school students attend Maine West High School in District 207.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Des Plaines housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts Des Plaines at 58,772 residents in its July 2025 estimate, down 3.1 percent from the April 2020 base. Most homes are owner-occupied, and a large share of residents were born abroad.

sections.h2: Does a river, tornado history or flooding matter when selling a Des Plaines house?
sections.html:
Yes, flood history matters to buyers and lenders. The city's well-known McDonald's museum was demolished in 2018 after repeated flooding, and the Des Plaines River runs just east of downtown. Disclose any basement water or past insurance claims and keep repair receipts.

Illinois recorded its earliest known tornado near modern Des Plaines in 1855, and spring storms can still be severe, with winter snow averaging about 38 inches a year at the nearby O'Hare station. Roofs, gutters, sump pumps and ejector pits are the items inspectors check most.

One more local quirk affects sellers: addresses inside city limits use the Des Plaines numbering system, while unincorporated parts of Maine Township with a Des Plaines mailing address follow Chicago's grid. Confirm with the city whether your parcel is incorporated, since that decides which city rules and which transfer tax apply.

sections.h2: How do Cook County recording and transfer taxes affect a Des Plaines sale?
sections.html:
Deeds for Des Plaines properties are recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. The clerk's fee schedule lists a deed at $107, which includes the GIS, document storage and rental housing support fees, and $5 per document for recording by mail with return.

Three transfer taxes can apply, and the Clerk's list shows the seller as the liable party on each:

  • State of Illinois: .50 per $500.00 of value, set by 35 ILCS 200/31-10 at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500.
  • Cook County: .25 per $500.00.
  • City of Des Plaines: 2.00 per $1,000.00, evidenced by a rubber stamp, with a $10.00 fee for exempt transfers.

The Clerk's municipal list states that its amounts are a courtesy and not legally binding, so ask the City of Des Plaines at 847-391-5325 to confirm the stamp before closing.

sections.h2: How are Des Plaines property taxes billed and appealed?
sections.html:
Cook County bills in two installments. The Treasurer's primer describes the first as 55 percent of the prior year's total tax, typically due March 1, with homeowner and senior exemptions reflected on the second installment bill. Late payments accrue interest at 1.5 percent per month.

The Cook County Assessor handles values. Maine Township, which includes parts of Des Plaines, was reassessed in 2025, and the Assessor released its values on June 4, 2025. Cook County follows a triennial cycle, so north suburban properties are not reassessed in 2026 unless something changes, such as a permit. Maine Township's 2026 window to file with the Assessor closed July 21, and the Board of Review window ran from August 31 to September 29, 2026.

Have the PIN ready when you talk to the Treasurer or Assessor, because Cook County identifies every parcel by a 14-digit number. Ask your closing agent how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What Des Plaines rules affect rentals and repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
Owners of rental property in Des Plaines must hold a rental license, and a 2009 ordinance requires them to complete Phase 1 of the Crime Free Multi-Housing Program. Anyone applying for a new rental license must take the seminar first.

For repairs, the city runs building permits through an online portal. Express permit guides cover sheds, decks, fences, driveways, roofs and non-structural kitchen and bathroom work. The city adopted the 2021 I-Codes, effective January 1, 2026, and its permit page lists construction hours of 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday. To schedule an inspection of a rental dwelling or work under permit, call 847-391-5382 or email permits@desplainesil.gov.

Closing out open permits before listing prevents a buyer's title search from turning up unfinished work.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when selling a Des Plaines house?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk's list shows the seller as liable for the state, county and city taxes. Your contract can allocate it differently, so confirm with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Des Plaines property?
faqs.a: With the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. Title companies can also submit deeds electronically.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to rent out my Des Plaines house?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental property owners must obtain a license and complete the Crime Free Multi-Housing seminar before a new license is issued.

faqs.q: Is my Des Plaines address inside the city?
faqs.a: Not always. Some unincorporated Maine Township addresses carry a Des Plaines mailing address but follow Chicago's numbering. Ask the city to confirm that your parcel is within the limits.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Maine Township assessment?
faqs.a: The 2026 filing windows with the Assessor and the Board of Review have closed. Cook County sets new windows by township each year, so check the Assessor's assessment calendar for the next opening.
